transcript.content: Hello. What brings you to the clinic today?
I just don’t care about any of the things I used to love doing anymore—not fishing, not cooking, not even singing at church. I just don't have the heart for any of it these days.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It’s been going on for about a year and a half now, starting not long after my wife passed away. This heavy, empty depression and not caring about anything has been with me pretty much every single day for a little over a year.
Have you ever experienced a similar period of deep sadness or loss of interest at any other time in your life, before your wife passed away?

No, I’ve never felt anything like this deep sadness before my wife passed away. Before she died, I was always active, busy with my handyman work, and heavily involved in my church and community. This whole empty feeling is completely new to me.
Along with feeling empty and losing interest, have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite during this time?

I hardly eat unless my sister drops food off, and even then I just pick at it because everything tastes like cardboard and my pants are hanging off me from losing so much weight. And at night, I mostly just lie awake with heavy thoughts, unable to really rest.
Have you been experiencing feelings of worthlessness, or strong feelings of guilt, perhaps blaming yourself for things related to your wife's passing or other matters?

No, I don't really blame myself for her passing, and I wouldn't say I feel worthless. I just feel incredibly empty and sad all the time. Sometimes I do feel like other people, like at the church or the hospital, are trying to punish me for something, but I don't feel that guilt myself.
Sometimes when people go through such a deep loss and feel this empty, they might have thoughts of wishing they were dead or thinking of ending their life. Have you had any thoughts like that?

To be honest, more nights than I'd like to admit, I lie in bed thinking it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. I've even caught myself picturing taking all of my blood pressure pills at once, though I haven't actually gone through with it.
You mentioned feeling like people at the church or hospital are trying to punish you. Could you tell me a bit more about why you feel that way and what you think they are doing?

I feel like some of the folks from the church and the hospital where my wife passed are watching me and trying to punish me. When the mail is late or the TV flickers, I take it as a sign they're keeping tabs on me or sending me messages. My sisters say it's just crazy talk, but it feels completely real to me.

That sounds incredibly stressful to go through, and sometimes severe grief can make our minds make connections that feel real but may not be. To help me understand, have you also heard any voices or seen things that others don't seem to notice?
No, I haven't heard any voices or seen things that aren't there. It's more that I just get this strong feeling of being watched, and I notice those signs like with the TV and the mail.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the criteria for a severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms (F32.3). He presents with persistent depressed mood, profound anhedonia, significant appetite and weight loss, insomnia, and active suicidal ideation with a conceptualized plan (overdosing on blood pressure medication), lasting for 1.5 years. Additionally, he exhibits persecutory delusions and delusions of reference (believing church and hospital staff are watching/punishing him, and interpreting late mail or TV flickering as signs). This is his first lifetime episode, ruling out recurrent depressive disorder.
